regime_context: The detector shows a broad but modestly rotating Canada/TSX landscape: 8 of 16 themes are eligible by the absolute-trend gate, with precious metals (Gold Miners, Silver & Royalties) holding the top two momentum ranks on decayed durability bars (0.73 and 0.67) and full breadth, while energy and financials sit mid-pack and most defensive/rate-sensitive themes are ineligible. Gate_helps is true on this market's history, so trend discipline has cut drawdown even without a return edge; rotation timing is display-only and cross-sectional rank-IC is weak, so any directional lean here is my own judgement, not an edge extracted from the ranks.
emerging_watch: Watching Pipelines & Midstream (rank 7, eligible, trend Hurst tag but breadth 0.0): a confirmed handoff would need breadth to lift decisively off zero in the next several sessions. The watch retires if Pipelines & Midstream stays below rank 8 with breadth still at zero for two consecutive weeks.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners is the ranked leader, eligible under the absolute-trend gate, with full breadth (1.0) and a durability bar (0.73) that has decayed but not collapsed. It is not crowded (z 0.65) and not a one-narrative top, so the leadership is broad rather than a fragile single-name blowoff. I lean overweight on trend continuation, naming only the trend-gate and breadth legs — momentum rank itself is a focus lens, not a forecast.
evidence: absolute-trend gate validated as risk control on this market (gate_helps true)
theses.dissent: Hurst_tag is mixed and r10 is slightly negative (-0.0664), so the recent 10-session path is already wobbling; gold miners are a levered beta to the gold price, and with unscheduled macro surprise share at 0.92, a geopolitics-driven unwind could hit precious metals first.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO closes below its 50-day average and lags the S&P/TSX by 3% over any rolling 10 sessions before the check-by date

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties
theses.thesis: Silver & Royalties sits second with a score close to the leader (1.998 vs 2.145) and full breadth, eligible under the trend gate. It carries a mean-revert Hurst tag, which tempers conviction, but the rotation margin to Gold Miners is small (0.147) and absorption is low (0.31), so this is a two-theme precious-metals leadership rather than a clean single-narrative setup. I treat the challenger as a closely-coupled cousin, not an independent call.
theses.dissent: Hurst_tag mean-revert and a slightly lower durability bar than Gold Miners suggest Silver & Royalties may chop around the leader rather than trend cleanly; royalty names embed credit and counterparty risk that can diverge from silver spot.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO (shared proxy) prints a lower 20-day return than the S&P/TSX while Silver & Royalties' relative score slips below rank 4 before the check-by date

theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: Oil & Gas Producers is eligible and ranked third, with respectable breadth (0.714) and a mixed-but-positive durability bar (0.63). It is the only crowded theme in the eligible set (crowding_z 1.2), which is a size-down caution, not a fade signal. The absolute-trend gate is the supporting leg here for staying long with discipline; the crowding flag argues for humility on how far this runs, not for exiting.
evidence: macro_narrative energy theme present but minor (n=3)
theses.dissent: Crowding at z 1.2 plus a heavy macro backdrop dominated by geopolitics with 0.92 unscheduled share means oil names are exposed to headline-driven supply shocks in either direction; the macro energy narrative is thin (n=3), so there is no supportive conviction from the news flow.

falsifier.text: XEG.TO trades below its 20-day average and lags the S&P/TSX by 4% over any rolling 10 sessions before the check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
